However, stale-cleanup safety is incomplete: cleanup IDs are recorded only when ConversationUnfollowed is emitted, so a delayed/origin replay can erase a post-re-add follow for a conversation created later, previously cleaned by the old implementation, or skipped because another group supplied access. The replay test first completes cleanup with the new token mechanism and therefore does not exercise this gap. A re-add is also authoritative immediately after its event commits while its caller merely waits for the cleanup handler, allowing another process to establish a follow before delayed removal cleanup erases it. Implement generation/version ordering that handles first delivery, historical replay, skipped/shared conversations, and this controlled remove/re-add/follow race. Additionally, consistency: :eventual currently bypasses the promised handler wait, and an event-free exact retry after a consistency timeout can report success without waiting for the original cleanup; preserve return modes while making completion durable in both cases. Handle successful {:ok, result} returns in clear_removed_group_member_follows/2 instead of crashing, and add the packet-required direct Admin system-group no-op coverage. I did not rerun the worker's passing commands because their exact current-state evidence is present; the deficiencies are semantic and absent from those tests.
